_doc: Terrain layer contract between tools/assetgen/textures/gen/terrain.py (generator) and the terrain shader. Slice i of every array = layers[i]; never reorder (append new layers at the end). tile_metres = real-world size of one texture repeat (UV = world_xz / tile_metres). The generator refuses to build the arrays if this file disagrees with it.

channels.terrain_albedo_array: Texture2DArray, 1024^2 slices. RGB = albedo (sRGB, sample with source_color), A = height 0..1 normalised per layer (mean ~0.5) for height-based blending.
channels.terrain_normal_array: Texture2DArray, tangent-space normal, OpenGL convention (+Y = green up), linear. Decode n = rgb * 2 - 1.
channels.terrain_orm_array: Texture2DArray, linear. R = ambient occlusion, G = roughness, B = metallic (always 0).
channels.terrain_macro_variation: Texture2D, linear, tileable. R = brightness (0.5 neutral; suggest albedo *= mix(0.8, 1.2, R)), G = warm/cool hue shift (0.5 neutral), B = damp/patch mask 0..1 (darken + gloss, or drive moss/wet blends), A = mid-scale breakup noise for dissolving height blends.
channels.terrain_detail_normal: Texture2D, tangent-space normal (OpenGL), imported as normal map, tileable micro detail (grit, crumbs, creases). Blend over every layer near the camera (e.g. fade out by ~15 m).

height_blend_contrast._doc: Suggested sharpness of the height blend per layer (higher = crisper transition into neighbours).

notes.concrete_slab: Saw-cut joints are baked on a 2 m grid aligned to the tile (joints at UV 0 and 0.5). Do not rotate/offset this layer with stochastic anti-tiling or the joints break.
notes.asphalt_cracked: Generic cracked town road (no lane markings: use decals). Tar crack-sealant bands are glossy (low roughness).
notes.mud: Standing water already sits in the deepest dents (flat normal, roughness ~0.05); the global hm_wetness can still darken/gloss the rest.
notes.rock_cliff: Water streaks run toward +V (down the texture rows); project with V pointing down the cliff.
notes.snow: Albedo is near-white (mean linear luminance 0.72); keep exposure/tonemapping in mind when blending.
